title: Composition of randomized runs
statement: Let $N$ and $M$ be nondeterministic Turing machines with Boolean symbols and respectively $K$ and $K'$ work tapes, on a fixed Boolean input $x$, and let $\phi$ map configurations of $N$ to configurations of $M$. Suppose that whenever a configuration $c$ of $N$ is not halted, one step of $M$ from $\phi(c)$ under any choice bit equals $\phi$ applied to the corresponding step of $N$. Suppose also that for some $m\in\mathbb{N}$, every length-$m$ choice word leaves $M$ halted when started from $\phi(c)$ whenever $c$ is halted; and that, for every halted $c$, the probability that $M$ satisfies a decidable predicate $Q$ after $m$ choice bits from $\phi(c)$ equals $g(o(c))$, where $o$ maps configurations of $N$ to Boolean values and $g$ maps Boolean values to rationals. Then, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and configuration $c$ of $N$ such that every length-$n$ choice word leaves $N$ halted, the probability that $M$ satisfies $Q$ after $n+m$ choice bits from $\phi(c)$ equals the probability that $o$ is true after $n$ choice bits of $N$ times $g(\mathrm{true})$, plus the probability that $o$ is false after $n$ choice bits of $N$ times $g(\mathrm{false})$.
